# Source tally

Generated by `scripts/gen_source_tally.py` (2026-11-21 18:43Z) at the end of every refresh; do not edit by hand. Built from out/coverage.json (2026-11-21T15:19:38Z), out/sources.json (2026-11-21T15:19:33Z), docs/source-checklist.json (1734 rows), data/sources/*.yaml (491 rows) and the water files.

What each state gives us and what it does not, so the opportunities stay in view. It is a map of sources, never a safety verdict: a state with few feeds is a state we read little of, not a clean one. States run New England then the mid-Atlantic. A source spanning several states is listed in each. `Unlock` says what it would take: an owner sign-up, an owner contact, a licence decision, a records request, a bot wall to get round, an image-only posting, no URL found, or engineering work; owner items link to the line in docs/owner-signups.md or docs/decisions.md.

## South Dakota (SD): Dated reports, delayed

Overflow reports from sewer operators in South Dakota are published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, but the newest is from Nov 2, 2026 and reports typically appear 8 days after a discharge; a quiet map in South Dakota can mean a report has not appeared yet.
